propositions: Gate operations (transition closed, review-plan, verify-completion) emit no stdout/stderr between start and final verdict, exceeding 600s silence windows common to supervisor stall watchdogs
Long-running gate calls are classified by design as feature-request (ADR 0089 defers stream-event idle watchdog behind async migration; test suite pins silence-tolerance as correct)
Silent phases include local compute (27s prologue, 40s overlap retrieval) unrelated to model latency, alongside model calls that represent ~9% of total wall clock
Supervisor stall detection cannot distinguish healthy multi-minute gate runs from hung processes, causing agents to be killed mid-close with epic/story left in_progress and descendants closed

Existing tests (test_no_total_runtime_timer_mechanism, test_slow_but_alive_server_completes_under_read_timeout) affirmatively encode silence-tolerance as correct, constraining any progress-emission fix to be purely additive and not introduce total-runtime caps

AC-2 requests documented expected duration range and interaction with supervisor stall budgets; remedy options include periodic progress heartbeat to stderr, streamed model interaction, or documentation warning that gate ops routinely exceed 600s budgets while silent
